value.rationale: The sampled principal angle is what experiments and discretely observed trajectories physically record; its variance is finite at fixed lag despite the divergent variance of the theoretical rational velocity. The exact rare-macroscopic-turn law and moment threshold quantify rare full-angle errors, and the unique coupling optimum solves the nontrivial operational tradeoff between driven rotational signal and thermal angular noise under fixed unequal temperatures. The complete profile and optimizer, not a generic calculus renaming, motivate this exact invariant. Limits: no energy-efficiency or long-time inference claim.
